deep.reconstruction:
Context (from the previous page): this is Riemann's second example in 'Beispiele von Flächen kleinsten Inhalts': a minimal surface bounded by two rectilinear polygons lying in parallel planes. The surface is doubly connected. Its Gauss image covers the sphere once. It is bounded by two families of great-circle arcs, whose planes are perpendicular to the polygon planes, meeting at the two poles. Stereographic projection from the tangent plane at one pole gives a region H in the eta-plane, where eta is the projected unit normal.

Step 1 (shape of H). H fills the eta-plane and is bounded on two sides.
- Inner boundary: a star of straight segments from eta=0 out to points A_1,...,A_n. These are the images of the normal arcs belonging to the sides of the first polygon; all its corners map to the pole eta=0.
- Outer boundary: a system of rays from points B_1',...,B_n' to eta=infinity. Their prolongations pass through the origin, so they are radial. They come from the second polygon, all of whose corners map to eta=infinity.
- Great circles through the poles project to lines through 0, which is why all boundary pieces are radial.
- The points A_i and B_i' are the 'Umkehrpunkte' of the normal along each side.
- The parenthetical remark is a hedge about the corners of the polygons (apparently a convexity-type proviso; the margin note on the previous page also concerns re-entrant corners).

Step 2 (uniformising the doubly connected region). Map H conformally onto a surface T_1 that covers the upper t-half-plane twice. The two boundary curves of H go to real values of t.
- Riemann–Hurwitz: a 2-sheeted cover of a disc with b branch points has Euler characteristic 2*1 - b. A doubly connected surface has chi = 0, so b = 2.
- Adding the mirror image (Schwarz reflection across the real axis) gives the closed double t-plane T_2. It has four branch points in conjugate pairs p, conj(p), q, conj(q).
- T_2 is a genus-1 (elliptic) Riemann surface, the Schottky double of the annulus.

Step 3 (normalisation). Replace t by t', linked to t by an equation quadratic in each variable. This is the Euler-type symmetric biquadratic relation of the elliptic addition theorem: it combines a real Möbius map with a translation along the real cycle of the elliptic curve.
- The branch points are placed at t' = ±i, ±i/kappa with kappa real. The curve is then w^2 = (1+t^2)(1+kappa^2 t^2), so Delta(t) = sqrt((1+t^2)(1+kappa^2 t^2)).
- In addition, one arbitrary real value of t can be sent to a prescribed real t' in one of the sheets.
- Parameter count (my addition):
  - A real Möbius map has 3 real parameters.
  - Sending p to i costs 2 conditions; putting the image of q on the imaginary axis costs 1. The real number kappa is then the conformal modulus of the annulus.
  - Möbius maps alone leave no freedom to fix an extra real point. The extra real parameter comes from the 1-parameter rotation group of the annulus, i.e. real translations on the torus. In t these are not Möbius but given by the (2,2) addition relation, which explains the word 'quadratische'.
  - The correction from 'zwei beliebigen' to 'einem beliebigen' is the right count.

Step 4 (statement of the problem). Determine t as a function of eta such that:
- t is single-valued and continuous on H;
- t is real on both boundary lines of H;
- (continued on the next page) a stated first-order behaviour holds at every point of the two boundary lines.

The next page then shows that d log eta/dt is single-valued on T, hence rational in t and Delta(t). This leads to an elliptic-integral representation of log eta, in the spirit of Schwarz–Christoffel.
errors: The same index n is used for the vertices of both boundary systems (A_1..A_n and B_1'..B_n'). This tacitly assumes both polygons have the same number of sides, which is not required in general; it is harmless as notation.
The parenthetical '(wenn nämlich die Ecken der beiden Polygone ... sind)' is incomplete or illegible. The proviso it states (presumably on the type of corners) is not made precise.

'Quadratische Gleichung in Bezug auf beide Variable' is terse. A pure real Möbius (bilinear) change of variable could not also fix an extra real point after the branch-point normalisation. The claim is correct only when the relation is read as the (2,2) addition-theorem correspondence (a translation on the elliptic curve), which Riemann evidently intends.
No real mathematical error otherwise; the topological count (two branch points for a doubly connected double cover of the half-plane, four after reflection) is correct.

results.what: Gauss map of a minimal surface bounded by two polygons in parallel planes, projected stereographically: a region bounded by radial slits from 0 and radial rays to infinity
results.modern_name: Weierstrass–Enneper representation / Gauss-map method for polygonal Plateau problems
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (published posthumously by Hattendorff, 1867/68); Weierstrass 1866; Schwarz

results.what: Double cover of the half-plane with two branch points for a doubly connected domain; reflection to a closed double plane with four conjugate branch points (genus 1)
results.modern_name: Schottky double of an annulus; Riemann–Hurwitz count; Schwarz reflection
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (Dirichlet-principle/Schottky-double ideas; Schottky 1877 for the double)

results.what: Normalisation of the branch points to ±i, ±i/kappa via a (2,2) correspondence, with one free real point
results.modern_name: Legendre/Jacobi normal form of an elliptic curve; conformal modulus of an annulus; translations via the Euler addition theorem
results.usually_credited_to: Legendre/Jacobi (normal form); Riemann for its use in the minimal-surface problem

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of material Hattendorff published from Riemann's Nachlass in 'Über die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung' (Abh. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 13, 1867/68; Werke). The doubly connected two-polygon example with elliptic functions is known as Riemann's. The draft adds only small details (the explicit parameter count and the deletions).

checkable.asserts: The branch points of Delta(t) are t = ±i and ±i/k.
The polynomial under the root has real coefficients, so the branch points come in conjugate pairs (reflection symmetry), with k real.
Riemann–Hurwitz: a doubly connected 2-sheeted cover of a disc has b = 2 branch points; after doubling there are 4, giving genus 1.
The (2,2) addition relation is a translation on the curve: it preserves the differential dt/Delta(t) and keeps real t real, giving the extra real parameter used in the normalisation.

checkable.sympy: f = (a*t+b)/(c*t+d); count real parameters: 4 - 1 = 3; conditions f(p)=I (2 real) + re(f(q))=0 (1 real) => 0 left
checkable.asserts: A real Möbius map alone cannot also fix an extra real point after normalising the branch points, which is why the quadratic correspondence is needed.

transcription_corrections: 'daher in ∞ Nullpunkt zusammenlaufen' should read 'daher im Nullpunkt zusammenlaufen' (the prolongations of the outer rays pass through the origin).

In the parenthetical, the image reads '(wenn nämlich die Ecken der beiden Polygone [?] sind)'; a word, possibly an adjective describing the corners, is illegible, so the remark is not complete as transcribed.

Line 5: 'unendlich fernen Punkte' is preceded by a deleted word; the inserted '{+von verschiedenen+}' sits above 'Punkte', i.e. 'nach dem unendlich fernen Punkte, von verschiedenen [Richtungen?]', partly illegible.
In the margin left of 'so zu bestimmen' there is a marginal symbol 'η' plus a mark, probably indicating the variable eta; the transcription omits it.
'Fläche T_2 [-mit-][-mit-] {+denn+}' should probably read '{+dann+}' or simply 'mit vier Verzweigungspunkten'.
In the sentence ending 'in jedem Punkt der beiden', 'Begrenzungsbogen' is likely 'Begrenzungslinien' (consistent with the next page).
